wu: Teacher greets students and shows a world map. Students point to their home country and say: 'I am from Morocco.' Teacher models and drills pronunciation.
wuAlt: Teacher holds up flag flashcards; students say the country name and nationality in chorus.
Teacher says a country; students jump and say the nationality.
pres: Teacher presents 5 country flashcards (Morocco, USA, UK, France, Spain) with flags and nationalities. Models 'He is from Morocco. She is from Spain.' Checks understanding with thumbs up/down for true/false sentences.
presAlt: Teacher draws simple country outlines on the board; students guess and repeat the country name.
Teacher uses a short video clip of people saying 'I am from...' with subtitles.
prac: Students work in pairs with a country table worksheet. They take turns asking 'Where are you from?' and answering 'I am from [country].' Teacher monitors and corrects errors.
pracAlt: Students play 'Find Someone Who...' with a grid of countries; they ask classmates and write names.
Teacher gives each student a country card; they mingle and ask 'Where are you from?' to the group.
ls: Students listen to a KET-style audio of 3 people introducing themselves. They complete a table with names and countries. Teacher plays audio twice.
re: Teacher calls out a country; students race to point to it on the world map. Fastest student gets to call the next country.
prod: Students stand in a circle. The first student says 'I am from Morocco.' The next student says 'He is from Morocco. I am from France.' The chain continues around the circle.
rw: Students read 3 short profiles (e.g., 'My name is Amina. I am from Morocco.') and fill in a table with countries. Then they write 3 sentences: 'He is from Spain. She is from France. I am from Morocco.'
st: Teacher sings a simple 'Where Are You From?' song with clapping. Class says goodbye with 'Thank you, teacher. See you next time!'
g: Students mingle, ask 'Where are you from?', and mark countries on their map.
Teacher describes a country (language, flag); students guess the name.
Students write nationalities on a grid; teacher calls them out.
Students sit in a circle; each adds a country to the growing list.
Students match country flags to their names on flashcards.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences about famous people's countries.
Support: Use word bank with countries/nationalities for writing task.
hw: Complete the 'Where Are You From?' survey with 5 family members.
Draw 3 flags and write the country names.
Write 3 sentences about your classmates from today's class.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references (e.g., 'I am from Morocco, like Hassan II.') to build connection and pride in the learners' identity while practicing the target language.
